topic: Driscoll-Holmer frame-rate independent exponential decay damper vs linear-dt lerp overshoot rig
topic_zh: Driscoll-Holmér 帧率无关精确指数衰减阻尼对比朴素 λ·Δt 线性插值速度漂移与卡顿过冲
scope: Deterministic Rory Driscoll (2016) & Freya Holmer (2024) frame-rate independent exponential decay damping (alpha = 1 - exp(-lambda * dt)) versus naive frame-dependent linear-dt lerp (alpha = lambda * dt) and 64-substep RK4 ODE integration across 17 frame-rate subdivision stations (N in [1, 17] over T = 0.25s). No neural camera stabilization execution.

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating Node CPU runs after warmup. Closed-form exponential decay stepper versus 64-step 4th-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) ODE integration.

protocol.function: α = 1 − exp(−λ·Δt) → Invariant x(0.25s) = 8.6466 m Across All 17 Frame Rates (0.0000 m Drift)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 frame-rate subdivision stations converge to identical 8.6466m position without hitch overshoot

good_fit: Smooth camera follow, UI value interpolation, audio/exposure adaptation, and turret tracking across variable 30Hz–240Hz displays
Preventing single-frame shader-compile or GC hitches (λ·Δt > 1) from flinging the camera past the target (+11.35m overshoot)
Exact semigroup invariance: splitting any interval Δt into N arbitrary substeps produces the exact same final state
Replacing fixed-step RK4 sub-stepping loops for first-order linear relaxation systems
not_for: Second-order spring-mass systems requiring intentional momentum overshoot and oscillation (use analytical underdamped springs)
Constant-speed linear motion (moveTowards(x, target, speed * dt)) where velocity is constant rather than proportional to distance
Neural video frame interpolation or optical-flow gimbal stabilization
